title.en: The Midwives and the Baby in the Ark of Bulrushes
title.zh: 收生婆與蘆葦箱中的嬰孩

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapters 1-2

summary.en: A Pharaoh 'which knew not Joseph' enslaves Israel and orders every Hebrew boy drowned in the river; the midwives Shiphrah and Puah fear God and disobey, telling him Hebrew women deliver before they arrive. A Levite mother hides her goodly son three months, then sets him in a slime-sealed ark of bulrushes among the flags, where Pharaoh's daughter finds him, has pity, and — through the quick tongue of his watchful sister — pays his own mother to nurse him, naming him Moses, 'because I drew him out of the water.'
summary.zh: 「不認識約瑟的新王」壓迫以色列，下令溺殺希伯來男嬰；收生婆施弗拉與普阿敬畏神而不從。利未女子藏子三月，後將其放入塗石漆石油的蘆葦箱，置於河邊蘆荻中。法老女兒發現嬰孩，動了憐憫之心；其姊機敏召來生母代哺。公主為其命名摩西——「因我把他從水裏拉出來」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition of Judaism and Christianity. The exposed-hero-on-water is presented alongside other river-escape birth narratives.

passages.text: And the king of Egypt spake to the Hebrew midwives, of which the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah: and he said, When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women; if it be a son, then ye shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then she shall live. But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive. Therefore God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty.

And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi. And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months. And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river's brink. And his sister stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him.

And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and when she saw the ark among the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it. And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews' children. Then said his sister to Pharaoh's daughter, Shall I go and call to thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee? And she called the child's mother. And the child grew, and she called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water.

title.en: Moses Slays the Egyptian and Flees to Midian
title.zh: 摩西殺埃及人而逃米甸

region.en: Egypt to Midian, by the well

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 2

summary.en: Grown up in Pharaoh's house but going out to look on his brethren's burdens, Moses kills an Egyptian smiting a Hebrew and hides him in the sand; the next day a Hebrew challenges him — 'who made thee a prince and a judge over us?' — and the deed is known, so he flees to Midian. At a well he drives off shepherds harassing Jethro's seven daughters, waters their flock, and marries Zipporah, naming his son Gershom, 'I have been a stranger in a strange land'; meanwhile Israel's cry rises to God, who remembers his covenant.
summary.zh: 摩西在法老宮中長大，卻出去看弟兄的重擔；見埃及人打希伯來人，便殺之藏於沙中。次日被同族揭破——「誰立你作我們的首領和審判官呢？」——遂逃往米甸。在井旁驅散欺凌葉忒羅七女之牧羊人，為其羊群飲水，娶西坡拉為妻，生子革舜——「我在外邦作了寄居的」。以色列人在捆鎖中歎息哀求，神記念祂的約。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Included as the fugitive-prince-to-shepherd phase of the hero cycle.

passages.text: And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown, that he went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens: and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren. And he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand. And he said, Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? intendest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian? And Moses feared, and said, Surely this thing is known. Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.

Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father's flock. And the shepherds came and drove them away: but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock. And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter. And she bare him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land. And it came to pass in process of time, that the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage, and their cry came up unto God by reason of the bondage. And God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.

title.en: The Burning Bush and the Name I AM
title.zh: 焚而不毀的荊棘與「自有永有者」

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapters 3-4

summary.en: Keeping Jethro's flock at Horeb, Moses turns aside to see why a bush burns and is not consumed, and the LORD calls from within it, appointing him to bring Israel out of Egypt into a land flowing with milk and honey. Moses' three refusals — Who am I? What is your name? I am slow of speech — are answered by 'I AM THAT I AM', three signs (rod to serpent, leprous hand, water to blood), and Aaron as his mouth; Jesus later grounds his own divine claims on this name.
summary.zh: 摩西牧羊至何烈山，見荊棘被火燒著卻未燒燬，便轉過去看；耶和華從荊棘裏呼叫，差他領以色列出埃及，入流奶與蜜之地。摩西三度推辭——我算甚麼？你叫甚麼名字？我拙口笨舌——神以「我是自有永有的」答之，並賜三個神蹟記號，以亞倫為其口。耶穌後來正是以此名自證其神聖身份。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The divine name is treated with reverence in both Judaism and Christianity; quoted here as public-domain scripture in a comparative framing.

passages.text: And the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed. And Moses said, I will now turn aside, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt. And when the LORD saw that he turned aside to see, God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses. And he said, Here am I. And he said, Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.

And the LORD said, I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows; and I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land unto a good land and a large, unto a land flowing with milk and honey. Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt.

And Moses said unto God, Behold, when I come unto the children of Israel, and shall say unto them, The God of your fathers hath sent me unto you; and they shall say to me, What is his name? what shall I say unto them? And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you. And the LORD said furthermore unto him, Put now thine hand into thy bosom. And he put his hand into his bosom: and when he took it out, behold, his hand was leprous as snow.

And Moses said unto the LORD, O my LORD, I am not eloquent, neither heretofore, nor since thou hast spoken unto thy servant: but I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue. And the LORD said unto him, Who hath made man's mouth? have not I the LORD? Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say. And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses, and he said, Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I know that he can speak well. And he shall be thy spokesman unto the people: and he shall be, even he shall be to thee instead of a mouth, and thou shalt be to him instead of God.

region.en: Wayside inn, road from Midian to Egypt

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 4

summary.en: One of scripture's strangest three verses: on the road back to Egypt the LORD meets Moses and seeks to kill him, until Zipporah takes a sharp stone, circumcises her son, and casts the foreskin at his feet — 'Surely a bloody husband art thou to me' — and so he lets him go. Commentators read it as the unfinished circumcision of Moses' son endangering the covenant-bearer; the blood rite averts the night attack.
summary.zh: 聖經中最奇異的三節經文：歸埃及途中，耶和華遇見摩西，想要殺他；西坡拉急取火石刀，為兒子行割禮，丟在摩西腳前說——「你真是我的血郎了」——神便放他。釋經者以為：未行割禮之子危及立約者之身，血禮解夜間之危。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. An obscure and much-debated episode; presented as a covenant-blood narrative.

passages.text: And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the LORD met him, and sought to kill him. Then Zipporah took a sharp stone, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me. So he let him go: then she said, A bloody husband thou art, because of the circumcision.

title.en: Let My People Go: Bricks Without Straw
title.zh: 容我的百姓去：無草製磚

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 5

summary.en: Moses and Aaron demand a three-day journey to sacrifice, and Pharaoh answers 'Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice? I know not the LORD, neither will I let Israel go' — then doubles the cruelty by cutting the straw supply while keeping the brick quota, so the officers are beaten and the people blame Moses. The tale of bricks made without straw became the proverb of impossible demands, and the crushed people turn on their deliverer: 'ye have made our savour to be abhorred.'
summary.zh: 摩西亞倫求三日行程往曠野獻祭；法老答「耶和華是誰，使我聽他的話？我不認識耶和華」——反下令不再供草，磚數如常，官長被責打，百姓怨懟摩西。「無草製磚」自此成為不可能之要求之成語；受壓的百姓反咬其拯救者：「你們使我們在法老眼前可憎。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Pharaoh's divine-king denial frames the contest of kingships.

passages.text: And afterward Moses and Aaron went in, and told Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness. And Pharaoh said, Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice to let Israel go? I know not the LORD, neither will I let Israel go. And the king of Egypt said unto them, Wherefore do ye, Moses and Aaron, let the people from their works? get you unto your burdens.

And Pharaoh commanded the same day the taskmasters of the people, and their officers, saying, Ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick, as heretofore: let them go and gather straw for themselves. And the tale of the bricks, which they did make heretofore, ye shall lay upon them; ye shall not diminish ought thereof: for they be idle. And the taskmasters hasted them, saying, Fulfil your works, your daily tasks, as when there was straw.

Then the officers of the children of Israel came and cried unto Pharaoh, saying, Wherefore dealest thou thus with thy servants? There is no straw given unto thy servants, and they say to us, Make brick: and, behold, thy servants are beaten; but the fault is in thine own people. But he said, Ye are idle, ye are idle: therefore ye say, Let us go and do sacrifice to the LORD. And they met Moses and Aaron, who stood in the way, as they came forth from Pharaoh: and they said unto them, The LORD look upon you, and judge; because ye have made our savour to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh.

title.en: Aaron's Rod Swallows the Sorcerers' Rods
title.zh: 亞倫的杖吞了術士的杖

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 7

summary.en: Before Pharaoh, Aaron casts down his rod and it becomes a serpent; the Egyptian wise men and sorcerers match the sign with their enchantments — 'but Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods.' The court duel of magic opens the plague cycle, and the hardened heart of Pharaoh begins its long, strange refrain.
summary.zh: 法老面前，亞倫丟杖變蛇；埃及的博士和術士也用邪術照樣而行——「但亞倫的杖吞了他們的杖」。這場法術對決揭開災禍的序幕；法老剛硬的心，自此成為奇特的反覆疊句。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Egyptian court sorcery is presented as the narrative foil, not endorsed; the witch tag follows the text's own category of enchanters.

passages.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying, When Pharaoh shall speak unto you, saying, Shew a miracle for you: then thou shalt say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and cast it before Pharaoh, and it shall become a serpent. And Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharaoh, and they did so as the LORD had commanded: and Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh, and before his servants, and it became a serpent.

Then Pharaoh also called the wise men and the sorcerers: now the magicians of Egypt, they also did in like manner with their enchantments. For they cast down every man his rod, and they became serpents: but Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods. And he hardened Pharaoh's heart, that he hearkened not unto them; as the LORD had said.

region.en: Land of Egypt, Nile to palace
region.zh: 埃及全地，尼羅河至王宮

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapters 7-10

summary.en: Blood turns the Nile to stench; frogs swarm into ovens and kneadingtroughs; dust becomes lice the magicians cannot copy — 'this is the finger of God'; flies divide Goshen from the palaces; murrain kills the cattle; boils break the magicians' standing; thunder, fire-mingled hail, locusts on the east wind, and a darkness 'which may be felt' for three days fall in turn, each answered by a partial concession and a re-hardened heart — 'that thou mayest know that there is none like me in all the earth.'
summary.zh: 尼羅河化為血腥；青蛙入爐灶揉麵盆；塵土變虱，術士不能複製——「這是神的手段」；成群蒼蠅分別歌珊與王宮；瘟疫斃牲畜；瘡使術士站不住；雷雹夾火；東風捲來蝗蟲；三日黑暗「似乎可以摸得著」。每一次半讓步之後心便再剛硬——「好叫你知道普天下沒有像我的」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The plague cycle is presented as narrative; modern scholarship reads it against Egyptian natural hazards without adjudicating the theological claim.

passages.text: And all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood. And the fish that was in the river died; and the river stank, and the Egyptians could not drink of the water of the river. And the LORD spake unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch forth thine hand with thy rod over the streams, over the rivers, and over the ponds, and cause frogs to come up upon the land of Egypt. And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt; and the frogs came up, and covered the land of Egypt. And the magicians did so with their enchantments, and brought up frogs upon the land of Egypt.

And Aaron stretched out his hand with his rod, and smote the dust of the earth, and it became lice in man, and in beast; all the dust of the land became lice throughout all the land of Egypt. And the magicians did so with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but they could not: so there were lice upon man, and upon beast. Then the magicians said unto Pharaoh, This is the finger of God: and Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he hearkened not unto them.

And Moses stretched forth his rod toward heaven: and the LORD sent thunder and hail, and the fire ran along upon the ground; and the LORD rained hail upon the land of Egypt. So there was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous, such as there was none like it in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation. Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, was there no hail. And Pharaoh sent, and called for Moses and Aaron, and said unto them, I have sinned this time: the LORD is righteous, and I and my people are wicked.

And Moses stretched forth his rod over the land of Egypt, and the LORD brought an east wind upon the land all that day, and all that night; and when it was morning, the east wind brought the locusts. For they covered the face of the whole earth, so that the land was darkened; and they did eat every herb of the land. And the LORD said unto Moses, Stretch out thine hand toward heaven, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness which may be felt. And there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days: they saw not one another, neither rose any from his place for three days: but all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.

title.en: The Passover and the Midnight Strike

region.en: Goshen and Egypt, night of the Exodus
region.zh: 歌珊與埃及，出埃及之夜

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapters 11-12

summary.en: Each household takes a lamb without blemish, kills it at evening, marks lintel and doorposts with hyssop-dipped blood, and eats it in haste — loins girded, staff in hand, unleavened bread and bitter herbs. At midnight the LORD smites all the firstborn of Egypt, from Pharaoh's throne-heir to the captive in the dungeon; there is not a house without one dead, and a weeping Egypt thrusts Israel out with jewels of silver and gold. 'It is the LORD's passover' becomes the founding feast, kept forever; Christians read the unblemished lamb's blood as foreshadowing Christ, 'our passover', and the Last Supper is a Passover meal.
summary.zh: 各家取無殘疾羔羊，傍晚宰殺，以牛膝草蘸血塗門楣門框，束腰拿杖急速而食——無酵餅、苦菜。半夜，耶和華擊殺埃及一切長子，自法老長子至牢中囚徒；無一家不死一人，埃及舉國大哭，催促以色列速速離去，並以金銀相贈。「這是耶和華的逾越節」成為永遠遵守的定例。基督教視無瑕疵羔羊之血預表基督——「我們逾越節的羔羊」，而主的晚餐正是一次逾越節筵席。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition central to Judaism (Passover) and Christianity (Last Supper typology); presented as ritual-origin narrative with both readings noted.

passages.text: In the tenth day of this month they shall take to them every man a lamb, according to the house of their fathers, a lamb for an house. Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year: ye shall take it out from the sheep, or from the goats: and ye shall keep it up until the fourteenth day of the same month: and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it in the evening. And they shall take of the blood, and strike it on the two side posts and on the upper door post of the houses, wherein they shall eat it.

And thus shall ye eat it; with your loins girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and ye shall eat it in haste: it is the LORD's passover. For I will pass through the land of Egypt this night, and will smite all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment: I am the LORD. And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.

And Moses called for all the elders of Israel, and said unto them, Draw out and take you a lamb according to your families, and kill the passover. And ye shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the bason, and strike the lintel and the two side posts with the blood that is in the bason; and none of you shall go out at the door of his house until the morning. And it came to pass, that at midnight the LORD smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive that was in the dungeon; and all the firstborn of cattle.

And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for there was not a house where there was not one dead. And he called for Moses and Aaron by night, and said, Rise up, and get you forth from among my people, both ye and the children of Israel; and go, serve the LORD, as ye have said. Also take your flocks and your herds, as ye have said, and be gone; and bless me also. And the people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneadingtroughs being bound up in their clothes upon their shoulders.

title.en: Pillar of Cloud and Fire, with the Bones of Joseph
title.zh: 雲柱火柱與約瑟的骸骨

region.en: Succoth to Etham, edge of the wilderness

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 13

summary.en: Rather than the short Philistine road and its war, God leads the harnessed people the long way by the wilderness of the Red Sea; Moses carries the bones of Joseph, honoring the oath of Genesis 50. The LORD goes before them by day in a pillar of cloud and by night in a pillar of fire — the visible presence that guides, shades, and lights the march.
summary.zh: 神不領百姓走近捷的非利士道路，恐怕他們遇戰而回，卻繞道紅海曠野而行；摩西攜約瑟骸骨同去，履行創世記末章的誓言。耶和華日間在雲柱中領路，夜間在火柱中光照——那可見的同在，引導、遮蔽、照看整支行列。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The cloud-and-fire presence is a classic theophany form.

passages.text: And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that God led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt: but God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red sea: and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt. And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.

And the LORD went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night: he took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people.

title.en: The Crossing of the Red Sea

region.en: Shore of the Red Sea, Egypt (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 紅海之濱，埃及（象徵性定位）

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 14

summary.en: Trapped between Pharaoh's six hundred chariots and the sea, Israel cries out — 'were there no graves in Egypt?' — and Moses answers the great line: 'Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD.' The angel and pillar of cloud move behind to darken the Egyptians; a strong east wind drives the sea back all night, and Israel crosses on dry ground with the waters a wall on either hand. The morning watch finds the chariot wheels dragging; the sea returns and covers the host — 'there remained not so much as one of them.'
summary.zh: 法老六百輛戰車迫近，以色列被夾於海與軍之間，哀呼「難道在埃及沒有墳地嗎？」摩西答以千古名句：「不要懼怕，只管站住，看耶和華今天向你們所要施行的救恩。」天使與雲柱移至其後；東風整夜吹海，海水分開，以色列行於乾地，水在他們左右作了牆垣。晨更時埃及車輪脫落，海水復合，全軍覆沒——「連一個也沒有剩下」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Presented as the central deliverance narrative of the Exodus cycle.

passages.text: And when Pharaoh drew nigh, the children of Israel lifted up their eyes, and, behold, the Egyptians marched after them; and they were sore afraid: and the children of Israel cried out unto the LORD. And they said unto Moses, Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness? And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever. The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.

And the angel of God, which went before the camp of Israel, removed and went behind them; and the pillar of the cloud went from before their face, and stood behind them: and it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel; and it was a cloud and darkness to them, but it gave light by night to these: so that the one came not near the other all the night. And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.

And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left. And the Egyptians pursued, and went in after them to the midst of the sea, even all Pharaoh's horses, his chariots, and his horsemen. And the LORD overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea. And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them. But the children of Israel walked upon dry land in the midst of the sea.

title.en: The Song of the Sea and Miriam's Timbrels
title.zh: 海之歌與米利暗的手鼓

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 15

summary.en: Moses and Israel sing the oldest poem in scripture: 'I will sing unto the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea... Who is like unto thee, O LORD, among the gods?' Miriam the prophetess takes a timbrel and all the women follow with dances, answering the refrain — the founding victory hymn of the tradition, sung and set to music from ancient liturgy to Handel.
summary.zh: 摩西與以色列眾人歌頌聖經中最古的詩篇：「我要歌頌耶和華，因他大大戰勝，將馬和騎馬的投在海中……耶和華啊，眾神之中誰能像你？」女先知米利暗手拿鼓，眾婦女隨她擊鼓跳舞應和——這是傳統的得勝之歌，自古禮儀至韓德爾的神劇，傳唱不絕。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The victory hymn is the founding song of the tradition.

passages.text: Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song unto the LORD, and spake, saying, I will sing unto the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea. The LORD is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation: he is my God, and I will prepare him an habitation; my father's God, and I will exalt him. The LORD is a man of war: the LORD is his name. Pharaoh's chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea: his chosen captains also are drowned in the Red sea.

Who is like unto thee, O LORD, among the gods? who is like thee, glorious in holiness, fearful in praises, doing wonders? Thou stretchedst out thy right hand, the earth swallowed them. Thou in thy mercy hast led forth the people which thou hast redeemed: thou hast guided them in thy strength unto thy holy habitation. The LORD shall reign for ever and ever.

And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances. And Miriam answered them, Sing ye to the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously; the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.

title.en: Bitter Waters Made Sweet at Marah

region.en: Marah and Elim, wilderness of Shur

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 15

summary.en: Three days without water end at Marah, whose springs are too bitter to drink; the people murmur 'What shall we drink?' and Moses cries to the LORD, who shows him a tree that, cast into the waters, makes them sweet. There the first wilderness statute is given — 'I am the LORD that healeth thee' — and Elim follows with its twelve wells and seventy palms, a green resting place on the edge of the desert.
summary.zh: 三日無水之後至瑪拉，水苦不能飲；百姓埋怨「我們喝甚麼呢？」摩西呼求耶和華，神指示一棵樹，丟入水中水就變甜了。在那裏頒下曠野第一條律例——「我耶和華是醫治你的」。隨後以琳有十二股水泉、七十棵棕樹，是曠野邊上的綠洲歇息處。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Wells-and-palms etiology of the wilderness stations.

passages.text: So Moses brought Israel from the Red sea, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water. And when they came to Marah, they could not drink of the waters of Marah, for they were bitter: therefore the name of it was called Marah. And the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink? And he cried unto the LORD; and the LORD shewed him a tree, which when he had cast into the waters, the waters were made sweet: there he made for them a statute and an ordinance, and there he proved them.

And said, If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the LORD thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his sight, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians: for I am the LORD that healeth thee. And they came to Elim, where were twelve wells of water, and threescore and ten palm trees: and they encamped there by the waters.

title.en: Bread from Heaven: Manna and Quails
title.zh: 天上來的糧：嗎哪與鵪鶉

region.en: Wilderness of Sin, between Elim and Sinai
region.zh: 汛的曠野，以琳與西奈之間

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 16

summary.en: Hunger makes the freed slaves dream of Egypt's fleshpots; the LORD rains bread from heaven, and quails cover the camp at evening. The small round thing 'as small as the hoar frost on the ground' is gathered an omer a head — he who gathered much had nothing over, and he who gathered little had no lack — breeding worms if hoarded, doubling on the sixth day, absent on the seventh: the daily bread that teaches the sabbath. An omer is laid up before the Testimony 'for your generations', and Israel eats manna forty years.
summary.zh: 饑餓使自由的奴隸懷念埃及的肉鍋；耶和華賜天糧，晚間鵪鶉飛來遮滿營地。早晨露水蒸發後，野地面上有如霜樣的小圓物——嗎哪。按飯量各取一俄梅珥——多收的沒有餘，少收的也沒有缺；留到早晨就生蟲變臭，第六日收雙份，第七日無。每天的分糧教曉安息日；一俄梅珥存於法櫃前「為後世代」，以色列吃嗎哪四十年。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The manna rule is the sabbath's first practical teaching; the omer pot is its memorial rite.

passages.text: And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness: and the children of Israel said unto them, Would to God we had died by the hand of the LORD in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots, and when we did eat bread to the full; for ye have brought us forth into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger. Then said the LORD unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.

And it came to pass, that at even the quails came up, and covered the camp: and in the morning the dew lay round about the host. And when the dew that lay was gone up, behold, upon the face of the wilderness there lay a small round thing, as small as the hoar frost on the ground. And when the children of Israel saw it, they said one to another, It is manna: for they wist not what it was. And Moses said unto them, This is the bread which the LORD hath given you to eat.

And when they did mete it with an omer, he that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack. And Moses said, Let no man leave of it till the morning. Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and stank. And it came to pass, that on the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for one man. And Moses said, To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the LORD: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning. Six days ye shall gather it; but on the seventh day, which is the sabbath, in it there shall be none.

And the house of Israel called the name thereof Manna: and it was like coriander seed, white; and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey. And Moses said, This is the thing which the LORD commandeth, Fill an omer of it to be kept for your generations; that they may see the bread wherewith I have fed you in the wilderness. As the LORD commanded Moses, so Aaron laid it up before the Testimony, to be kept. And the children of Israel did eat manna forty years, until they came to a land inhabited.

title.en: Water from the Rock at Massah and Meribah

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 17

summary.en: Thirst drives the people to stone-throwing mutiny — 'Is the LORD among us, or not?' — and God answers by standing on the rock in Horeb for Moses to strike: water gushes for the people and cattle. The place is named Massah and Meribah, temptation and strife, the standing etiology of both a spring and the sin of testing God.
summary.zh: 乾渴令百姓幾乎用石頭打死摩西——「耶和華是在我們中間不是？」神答以：祂要站在何烈山的磐石那裏，摩西擊打磐石，水就從磐石流出，使百姓和牲畜都喝。那地方名叫瑪撒（試探）、米利巴（爭鬧）——一處水泉與一宗試探神之罪的永久起源。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Rock-spring etiology; Paul later reads the rock as a type of Christ.

passages.text: And there was no water for the people to drink. Wherefore the people did chide with Moses, and said, Give us water that we may drink. And the people thirsted there for water; and the people murmured against Moses, and said, Wherefore is this that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst? And Moses cried unto the LORD, saying, What shall I do unto this people? they be almost ready to stone me.

And the LORD said unto Moses, Go on before the people, and take with thee of the elders of Israel; and thy rod, wherewith thou smotest the river, take in thine hand, and go. Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink. And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel. And he called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the chiding of the children of Israel, and because they tempted the LORD, saying, Is the LORD among us, or not?

title.en: Amalek and the Hands Held Up
title.zh: 亞瑪力之戰與舉手之禱

region.en: Top of the hill at Rephidim

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 17

summary.en: Amalek attacks Israel in the wilderness, and Moses, enthroned on a stone at the hilltop with the rod of God, raises his hands — while they are held up Israel prevails, when they drop Amalek does; Aaron and Hur steady the weary arms until sunset. Joshua wins the battle with the sword; the victory is written in a book, an altar is named Jehovahnissi — the LORD my banner — and war with Amalek is sworn 'from generation to generation.'
summary.zh: 亞瑪力人在曠野攻擊以色列。摩西手握神的杖登上山頂，坐在石頭上舉手——手舉起以色列就得勝，手下垂亞瑪力就得勝；亞倫與戶珥扶住疲憊的雙臂直到日落。約瑟夫——約書亞以刀劍得勝；戰績寫於書上，築壇名耶和華尼西——耶和華是我旌旗——並起誓必世世代代與亞瑪力人爭戰。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The eternal-war clause against Amalek has a heavy later interpretive history; presented as text, with the raised-hands intercession the episode's most-cited element.

passages.text: Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim. And Moses said unto Joshua, Choose us out men, and go out, fight with Amalek: to morrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the rod of God in mine hand. And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.

But Moses' hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun. And Joshua discomfited Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword. And Moses built an altar, and called the name of it Jehovahnissi: for he said, Because the LORD hath sworn that the LORD will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.

title.en: Jethro's Counsel: Judges by Thousands and Tens
title.zh: 葉忒羅獻策：設立千夫長

region.en: Camp before the mount of God

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 18

summary.en: Jethro arrives with Zipporah and the boys, hears the Exodus story, blesses the LORD — 'now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods' — and sacrifices with the elders. Watching Moses judge the people alone from morning to evening, the old priest of Midian delivers the classic counsel of delegation: able men who fear God as rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens; hard cases only to Moses. Moses hears him, and the judicial structure of Israel is born from a foreign father-in-law's advice.
summary.zh: 葉忒羅攜西坡拉與二子來見，聽出埃及之事，稱頌耶和華——「我如今知道耶和華比萬神都大」——並與長老同席獻祭。見摩西自朝至暮獨自審判百姓，這位米甸老祭司獻上授權分層的千古良策：選敬畏神、誠實無妄之人作千夫長、百夫長、五十夫長、十夫長；難斷之事才呈摩西。以色列司法制度自此而生，竟出於異邦岳父之口。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The first judicial hierarchy of Israel, credited to a Midianite priest.

passages.text: And Jethro rejoiced for all the goodness which the LORD had done to Israel, whom he had delivered out of the hand of the Egyptians. And Jethro said, Blessed be the LORD, who hath delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of Pharaoh. Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods: for in the thing wherein they dealt proudly he was above them. And Jethro, Moses' father in law, took a burnt offering and sacrifices for God: and Aaron came, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with Moses' father in law before God.

And when Moses' father in law saw all that he did to the people, he said, What is this thing that thou doest to the people? why sittest thou thyself alone, and all the people stand by thee from morning unto even? And Moses' father in law said unto him, The thing that thou doest is not good. Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for this thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.

Moreover thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens: and let them judge the people at all seasons: and it shall be, that every great matter they shall bring unto thee, but every small matter they shall judge: so shall it be easier for thyself, and they shall bear the burden with thee. So Moses hearkened to the voice of his father in law, and did all that he had said.

title.en: Thunder and Law at Mount Sinai

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapters 19-20

summary.en: On the third day, with the people washed and fenced off from the mount under pain of death, thunder and lightning, a thick cloud, a trumpet exceeding loud, and a trembling mountain: 'the LORD descended upon it in fire, and the smoke thereof ascended as the smoke of a furnace.' From the mount God speaks the Ten Commandments — no other gods, no graven image, no vain name, the sabbath, honour of parents, the four 'thou shalt nots' of killing, adultery, theft, false witness, and no coveting — until the terrified people beg Moses: 'Speak thou with us... but let not God speak with us, lest we die.'
summary.zh: 第三日，雷轟閃電、密雲遍山、角聲甚大，全營盡皆發顫；「耶和華在火中降於山上，山的煙氣上騰，如燒窯一般」。神從山上宣講十誡——除我以外不可有別神、不可拜偶像、不可妄稱神名、守安息日、當孝敬父母、不可殺人、姦淫、偷盜、作假見證、不可貪婪——百姓戰兢求摩西：「求你和我們說話……不要神和我們說話，恐怕我們死亡。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition central to Judaism and Christianity. The Decalogue is quoted as public-domain scripture in comparative framing.

passages.text: And it came to pass on the third day in the morning, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud upon the mount, and the voice of the trumpet exceeding loud; so that all the people that was in the camp trembled. And mount Sinai was altogether on a smoke, because the LORD descended upon it in fire: and the smoke thereof ascended as the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mount quaked greatly. And when the voice of the trumpet sounded long, and waxed louder and louder, Moses spake, and God answered him by a voice.

And God spake all these words, saying, I am the LORD thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. Thou shalt have no other gods before me. Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth. Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain. Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.

Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee. Thou shalt not kill. Thou shalt not commit adultery. Thou shalt not steal. Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour. Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour's.

And all the people saw the thunderings, and the lightnings, and the noise of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking: and when the people saw it, they removed, and stood afar off. And they said unto Moses, Speak thou with us, and we will hear: but let not God speak with us, lest we die. And Moses said unto the people, Fear not: for God is come to prove you, and that his fear may be before your faces, that ye sin not. And the people stood afar off, and Moses drew near unto the thick darkness where God was.

title.en: The Golden Calf and the Broken Tables

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapter 32

summary.en: With Moses forty days on the mount, the people demand of Aaron 'Up, make us gods which shall go before us'; the golden earrings of the women go into the fire and out comes a molten calf — 'These be thy gods, O Israel' — with a feast, eating, drinking, and playing. God offers to consume them and make a nation of Moses, who pleads for his people by the oath sworn to Abraham and turns the LORD from his wrath. Coming down with the tables written by the finger of God, he sees the calf, shatters the tables at the mount's foot, burns and powders the idol into the drinking water, and the sons of Levi — 'Who is on the LORD's side?' — put three thousand men to the sword; Moses offers to be blotted out of God's book for his people.
summary.zh: 摩西四十日未下山，百姓聚集對亞倫說：「起來，為我們作神像在我們前面引路。」眾人的金耳環入火，出來一隻金牛犢——「以色列啊，這是領你出埃及地的神」——築壇獻祭，坐下吃喝，起來玩耍。神欲滅絕之而另立摩西為大國；摩西以向亞伯拉罕所起的誓代求，神回心轉意。摩西攜神手所寫之石版下山，見犢像怒碎其版於山下，將金牛焚燒磨成粉末撒在水面上叫以色列人喝。利未子孫聞「凡屬耶和華的，都要到我這裏來」，當日殺約三千人。摩西甚至求從神冊上塗抹己名以贖民罪。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The idol-making episode is the paradigmatic transgression narrative; the internal violence is part of the text, presented without endorsement.

passages.text: And when the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, the people gathered themselves together unto Aaron, and said unto him, Up, make us gods, which shall go before us. And Aaron said unto them, Break off the golden earrings, which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters, and bring them unto me. And he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf: and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. And they rose up early on the morrow, and offered burnt offerings, and brought peace offerings; and the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.

And the LORD said unto Moses, Go, get thee down; for thy people, which thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves. Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation. And Moses besought the LORD his God, and said, LORD, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, which thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a mighty hand? Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, thy servants, to whom thou swarest by thine own self. And the LORD repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people.

And it came to pass, as soon as he came nigh unto the camp, that he saw the calf, and the dancing: and Moses' anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount. And he took the calf which they had made, and burnt it in the fire, and ground it to powder, and strawed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it. And Moses said, Who is on the LORD's side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him. And there fell of the people that day about three thousand men.

And it came to pass on the morrow, that Moses said unto the people, Ye have sinned a great sin: and now I will go up unto the LORD; peradventure I shall make an atonement for your sin. And Moses returned unto the LORD, and said, Oh, this people have sinned a great sin, and have made them gods of gold. Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin--; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written. And the LORD said unto Moses, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.

title.en: Show Me Thy Glory: Moses in the Cleft of the Rock
title.zh: 求你顯出你的榮耀：磐石穴中的摩西

region.en: Tent of meeting and cleft rock, Sinai

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 2: Exodus, chapters 33-34

summary.en: After the calf, God threatens to send an angel instead of himself; Moses pitches the tent of meeting outside the camp, where the LORD speaks with him 'face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend.' Bold from grace, Moses asks, 'I beseech thee, shew me thy glory'; he is hidden in a cleft of the rock, covered by the divine hand, and allowed to see only the back parts — 'for there shall no man see me, and live.' Renewing the tables, the LORD proclaims his name: 'The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering...' and when Moses descends, the skin of his face shines so that the people are afraid, and he wears a veil.
summary.zh: 金牛犢事件後，神揚言遣使者代行；摩西在營外支搭會幕，耶和華在那裏與他面對面說話，如人與朋友說話。摩西膽敢求告：「求你顯出你的榮耀。」神將他藏在磐石穴中，用手遮蔽，只許他看見神的背——「因為人見我的面不能存活」。重鑿法版之際，耶和華宣告己名：「耶和華，耶和華，是有憐憫有恩典的神，不輕易發怒……」摩西下山時，面皮因與神說話而發光，百姓懼怕，他便用帕子蒙臉。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The veiled shining face is among the most-cited theophany texts in Christian interpretation (2 Corinthians 3).

passages.text: And it came to pass, as Moses entered into the tabernacle, the cloudy pillar descended, and stood at the door of the tabernacle, and the Lord talked with Moses. And all the people saw the cloudy pillar stand at the tabernacle door: and all the people rose up and worshipped, every man in his tent door. And the LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend.

And he said, I beseech thee, shew me thy glory. And he said, I will make all my goodness pass before thee, and I will proclaim the name of the LORD before thee. And he said, Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live. And the LORD said, Behold, there is a place by me, and thou shalt stand upon a rock: and it shall come to pass, while my glory passeth by, that I will put thee in a clift of the rock, and will cover thee with my hand while I pass by: and I will take away mine hand, and thou shalt see my back parts: but my face shall not be seen.

And the LORD descended in the cloud, and stood with him there, and proclaimed the name of the LORD. And the LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed, The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth, keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty. And Moses made haste, and bowed his head toward the earth, and worshipped.

And he was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights; he did neither eat bread, nor drink water. And he wrote upon the tables the words of the covenant, the ten commandments. And it came to pass, when Moses came down from mount Sinai with the two tables of testimony in Moses' hand, when he came down from the mount, that Moses wist not that the skin of his face shone while he talked with him. And when Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come nigh him.
